(D)uplicate (D)oses Rate

Source: R/dd_rate.R
dd_rate.Rd

This function calculates the percentage of records in the electronic immunization registry (EIR) that are duplicate doses, that is, doses entered more than once by mistake, as opposed to programmatic errors where a dose is really administered twice. Results can be disaggregated by geographic level and by one additional variable.

Usage

dd_rate(
  data.EIR,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  disaggregate_by = NULL,
  vaccines = NULL,
  birth_cohorts = NULL
)

Arguments

data.EIR

Data frame. A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See immunABC.EIR for expected structure.

geo_level

Character. The geographic level to aggregate results by. Must be "ADM0", "ADM1" or "ADM2". If not specified, the default is "ADM0".

disaggregate_by

Character (optional). One additional variable to disaggregate results by: "dose" or "birth_cohort" (year of birth). If NULL (default), there is no additional disaggregation.

vaccines

Character (optional). A character vector specifying the doses to include in the analysis. This is only a filter: use disaggregate_by = "dose" to disaggregate results by dose. If NULL (default), all doses in data.EIR are included.

birth_cohorts

Numeric (optional). A vector specifying the birth cohort(s) for which the rate should be calculated. This is only a filter: use disaggregate_by = "birth_cohort" to disaggregate results by cohort. If NULL (default), all available cohorts are used.

Value

A data frame with one row for each duplication category in each group, with the following columns:

  • ADM1, ADM2: the geographic area of occurrence, depending on geo_level.

  • dose or birth_cohort: depending on disaggregate_by.

  • duplication: the category of each record, one of:

    • DUPLICATE: a duplicate record because all the columns match (ID, dose, vaccination date and place of ocurrence).

    • REPEATED: a repeated dose where only the ID and dose match, but the date of vaccination or the place of ocurrence are different. May be caused by programmatic errors or by data entry errors.

  • n: number of records in that category.

  • total: total number of evaluated records in the group.

  • rate: percentage of records in that category (n / total * 100).

Details

Records of the same person and dose are compared in date order. The first one is not counted, since it is considered the legitimate record, and each later one is classified as either DUPLICATE or REPEATED. Only extra records are counted, so a dose registered three times counts as two. For example, the same dose registered 3 times, once on January 5, another on February 10 and once again on February 10 would count as:

  • January 5: First dose, assumed to be legitimate.

  • February 10: REPEATED dose, because it is the same dose on a different date.

  • February 10: DUPLICATE dose, because it is registered on the same date as the previous.

Records missing ID, dose, date_vax, ADM1_occurrence or ADM2_occurrence do not contain sufficient information to determine if they are DUPLICATE or REPEATED, so they are filtered out. NA and empty or whitespace-only text count as missing. When using disaggregate_by = "birth_cohort", records with no date_birth are also filtered out, with a message. Finally, please note that in this analysis, geographic areas always refer to the place of occurrence of the vaccination event.
